versions.provenance: 8th edition lung (NSCLC) TNM, rewritten from criteria published on Medscape/public references; interim content pending the licensed content and R1 clinical verification.
versions.introduction:
The 8th edition staging system applies to non-small cell lung carcinoma; the same TNM is also applied to small cell lung cancer and bronchopulmonary carcinoid. T is driven mainly by tumour size in centimetres plus local invasion and separate tumour nodules, N by the location and laterality of involved intrathoracic nodes, and M by intrathoracic spread (M1a) versus a single (M1b) or multiple (M1c) extrathoracic metastases.

Compared with the 7th Edition, 8th edition introduced finer size-based T subcategories and split distant disease into M1a, M1b and M1c. Note that this is the 8th edition, not the later IASLC/UICC 9th Edition: in the 8th Edition N2 and M1c are not subdivided (the N2a/N2b and M1c1/M1c2 subcategories belong to the newer 9th Edition revision).

t.label: Primary tumour cannot be assessed, or tumour proven by malignant cells in sputum or bronchial washings but not visualised by imaging or bronchoscopy
Carcinoma in situ (squamous cell carcinoma in situ or adenocarcinoma in situ)
Tumour <= 3 cm in greatest dimension, surrounded by lung or visceral pleura, without bronchoscopic evidence of invasion more proximal than the lobar bronchus (not in the main bronchus)
Minimally invasive adenocarcinoma: adenocarcinoma <= 3 cm with a predominantly lepidic pattern and <= 5 mm of invasion
Tumour > 1 cm but <= 2 cm in greatest dimension
Tumour > 2 cm but <= 3 cm in greatest dimension

Tumour > 3 cm but <= 5 cm; or tumour that involves the main bronchus regardless of distance to the carina but without involving the carina, invades the visceral pleura, or is associated with atelectasis or obstructive pneumonitis extending to the hilar region involving part or all of the lung
Tumour > 3 cm but <= 4 cm in greatest dimension
Tumour > 4 cm but <= 5 cm in greatest dimension

Tumour > 5 cm but <= 7 cm; or directly invades any of the parietal pleura, chest wall (including superior sulcus tumours), phrenic nerve, or parietal pericardium; or separate tumour nodule(s) in the same lobe as the primary

Tumour > 7 cm; or invades any of the diaphragm, mediastinum, heart, great vessels, trachea, recurrent laryngeal nerve, oesophagus, vertebral body, or carina; or separate tumour nodule(s) in a different ipsilateral lobe from the primary

n.label: Regional lymph nodes cannot be assessed
Metastasis in ipsilateral peribronchial and/or ipsilateral hilar lymph nodes and intrapulmonary nodes, including involvement by direct extension
Metastasis in ipsilateral mediastinal and/or subcarinal lymph node(s)
Metastasis in contralateral mediastinal, contralateral hilar, ipsilateral or contralateral scalene, or supraclavicular lymph node(s)

m.label: Separate tumour nodule(s) in a contralateral lobe; tumour with pleural or pericardial nodules; or malignant pleural or pericardial effusion
Single extrathoracic metastasis in a single distant organ (including a single non-regional node)
Multiple extrathoracic metastases in one or several organs

stageGroups.basis: Malignant cells in sputum/washings, tumour not visualised
Intrathoracic spread or single extrathoracic metastasis

versions.regionalNodes: Intrathoracic lymph nodes classified by the IASLC nodal map, including ipsilateral peribronchial and intrapulmonary nodes and ipsilateral hilar nodes (N1); ipsilateral mediastinal and subcarinal nodes (N2); and contralateral mediastinal or hilar, ipsilateral or contralateral scalene, and supraclavicular nodes (N3). Laterality (ipsilateral versus contralateral) is what separates N1/N2 from N3.
versions.histologicGrade: GX to G4 (well to undifferentiated). For invasive non-mucinous adenocarcinoma, a pattern-based grade (predominant histologic pattern plus the proportion of any high-grade pattern) is increasingly used; squamous cell carcinoma is graded by degree of keratinisation and differentiation.
versions.histopathologicTypes: Non-small cell lung cancer comprises adenocarcinoma (most common), squamous cell carcinoma, and large cell carcinoma, with adenosquamous and sarcomatoid carcinomas less often. Small cell lung carcinoma and bronchopulmonary carcinoid are staged with the same TNM but are distinct entities.
prognosticFactors: Actionable molecular alterations (EGFR, ALK, ROS1, BRAF, MET, RET, KRAS and others)
